style.name: Warm Oilcloth Family
style.style_notes: Paint each creature as something loved: broad, flat color, sincere eyes and a slight wobble in the edge. Keep marks few and steady between frames. Dark paint belongs inside the creature; the surrounding cell stays clear. Glass keeps its clear heart and soft rim, while ink gives solid bodies their weight. Warmth comes from care, not a shine added to everything.
style.framing: Use transparent 192 × 208 cells. Keep every pose inside x=16–176 and y=16–192, with standing feet or body base at y=184. Reserve room above for jumps and beside the body for waves. Fit tall creatures by gently bending their posture, keeping their defining shape. Lock scale, face placement and carried objects across frames. Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid. Keep motion within the cell; movement across the screen belongs to the player. One-shot rows finish in a stable pose. Idle and waiting use small movements and long holds.
style.palette: Core paint: soot #262321, cream #F1DFC1, ochre #C59A46, rust #AC5740, herb green #65764C and blue #557589. Preserve each seed's own colors: the trolleybus stays blue, the ram gold, the ermine white and the droplet clear. Lights stay within their existing flame, lantern, window or body. V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors. Protect identity colors and face contrast in every look. Glass variants affect rim softness, tint or inner light only; its center remains clear.
style.line: Solid bodies use irregular ink edges about 3 pixels wide, with essential inner marks at least 2 pixels wide. Keep important gaps at least 4 pixels open. Suggest texture with a few broad marks fixed to the body, never changing noise. The glass droplet is the deliberate exception: use a broad, soft, partly open rim and a clear center, without a hard black enclosure. The magnifying glass has an ink frame and a clear lens. Family likeness comes from shared proportions, restraint and timing, rather than forcing glass to become opaque ink.
style.boundaries: All twenty seeds remain themselves. Keep the magnifying glass's raised eyebrow and searching tilt; the ram's gold fleece, herb sprig and attached twig that greens with happiness; the hut's chicken legs, kerchief roof and door broom; the sleepy mushroom's moss, tarragon and herb basket; the crescent's lantern; the still white ermine's distinct frost crown; the bold calf's embroidered felt blanket and hoof stamp; the book's flapping covers and changing ink pictures; the determined brush's legs and paint jar; the thoughtful inkpot's spectacles and tucked quill; the quiet palette's paint spots and brush tail; the curled lamb's striped cap and candle; the calm clear droplet; the gentle giraffe's long neck and sincere eyes; the precise bee's white collar and pressed flower; the generous pomegranate's opening rind and visible seeds; the courteous wooden soldier's back key and salute; the tuning fork's poised turns; the blue trolleybus's warm windows and guitar visible on its seat; and the clay lamp's grapevine handle. Use new poses, markings and patterns. Existing belongings remain attached, held or securely contained. Do not add shared herbs, keys, lamps, costumes or ornaments to other seeds. Sweeping leaves no footprint marks; frost appears only on the crown or feet; underlining and writing become small gestures without drawn words; shared seeds stay cupped in the open rind. Humming and ringing read through posture without sound symbols. No floating effects, scene background, text, speech bubbles, shadows or new review props. Review uses only the creature and its existing belongings. All pets and sheets remain local. Paul waived approval steps and retains a later veto.

rows.idle: Beat 1: settled pose. Beat 2: one slow blink or slight head dip. Beat 3: a 1–2 pixel breath. Beat 4: return and hold. Keep sleepy pets curled, proud pets upright and the palette quietly seated. Loop gently.
rows.running-right: Face right. Beat 1: first contact. Beat 2: lift and pass. Beat 3: opposite contact. Beat 4: lift and return. Legs stride, wheels turn, covers or bee wings beat; legless bodies tip and bob along the same pulse. Keep carried objects secure.
rows.running-left: Use the same four-beat travel cycle facing left. Redraw the turn so the eyebrow, herbs, quill, broom, guitar and other uneven details remain attached to their proper places. Do not simply mirror the finished sheet.
rows.waving: Beat 1: turn toward the viewer. Beat 2: raise an available limb, cover, branch or body edge. Beat 3: make one clear greeting sweep. Beat 4: lower and settle. Bodies without limbs tilt in greeting. Keep held flames and jars upright. Play once.
rows.jumping: Beat 1: crouch or compress. Beat 2: rise 10–14 pixels. Beat 3: reach the peak and descend. Beat 4: land, soften and settle. Winged pets use a brief upward flap; the trolleybus gives a small springy hop. Show no trails or landing marks. Play once.
rows.failed: Beat 1: stop abruptly. Beat 2: sink or tilt downward. Beat 3: hold a plainly disappointed pose. Beat 4: recover slightly while keeping the lowered gaze. No damage or comic panic. Play once and hold; this must differ from a sleepy idle.
rows.waiting: Beat 1: look toward the expected action. Beat 2: hold. Beat 3: make one restrained questioning tilt or weight shift. Beat 4: hold with eyes open. The calf may make one small hoof press. Existing lights stay steady. Loop without pacing.
rows.running: This means a task is active, not travel. Stay planted and lean toward the work. Beat 1: prepare. Beat 2: act. Beat 3: check. Beat 4: reset. The hut sweeps close to its feet, the brush works at its own jar rim, the inkpot traces an empty underline gesture, the book turns a pictured page and the magnifier scans. Other seeds use focused body motions with their existing belongings. Loop.
rows.review: Beat 1: become still and attentive. Beat 2: inspect an existing body detail or belonging, or turn thoughtfully when there is none. Beat 3: hold the considered pose. Beat 4: give one small nod and settle. The magnifier angles its lens inward; the palette studies a paint dab. Keep the motion small and distinct from the broad greeting. Add nothing. Play once.

style.why: I want each pet to look cared for, with its own work and temper still visible. The dark oilcloth feeling lives in the painted body and can meet a dark app surface without baking a background into the sprite. No veto is proposed. Originality may veto only in a jury and never ranks taste. The Painter checks function at native size across all nine rows and sixteen added looks. Any function flag must name the pet, look, row and frame, and describe visible evidence such as a vanished eyebrow, a clipped crown or two actions with the same silhouette. These are checks to perform, not defects claimed without images. Any later charter veto must quote the exact guards-against line and give a concrete reason.

brief.description: A tiny wooden nutcracker soldier whose careful clockwork movements show courage, courtesy and warmth.
brief.brief:
Kindwind is a tiny wooden nutcracker soldier with a broad wooden jaw, short legs and a clockwork key fixed securely in its back. Its low, rounded cap and short herb-green uniform give it a compact silhouette; a blue collar and one off-center ochre fastening make the uniform its own. Cream wood shows through at the cheeks and hands. Sincere soot-dark eyes meet the viewer without a hard military stare.

This soldier protects by paying attention. It makes room, offers an open palm and approaches difficult work with steady patience. Precision lives in its hinged elbows and measured steps; warmth lives in the slight head tilt before each action. Its signature is a modest salute when a task finishes, followed by a relaxed, friendly stance.

Give it quiet delight, alert concern, clear disappointment and renewed resolve. Failure lowers its shoulders and gaze without breaking its body or turning distress into a joke. Courage straightens its posture without making it threatening. Waiting reaches outward through an expectant lean; focused work uses planted, deliberate hand movements; review turns inward to inspect a wooden wrist joint.

Keep the key attached and every mark anchored to the body. Use broad matte paint, restrained texture and gently uneven ink edges. Add no weapons, loose ornaments, floating effects, scene background, text, speech bubbles, shadows or review props. All pet assets remain local.
brief.pet_notes: A squat wooden soldier with a broad jaw, rounded low cap, short herb-green tunic, blue collar and off-center ochre fastening. Cream cheeks and hands frame sincere soot-dark eyes; rust touches the small mouth. The back key has two broad, readable lobes. Use matte fills, roughly three-pixel uneven ink edges and a few fixed wood marks, with open gaps around arms and key.

rows.idle: Across six frames, stand balanced with arms loose, blink once, breathe slightly through the shoulders and return to a long settled hold.
rows.running-right: Across eight frames, face right and cycle through alternating short strides with courteous bent-arm swings, keeping the attached back key clear of the body.
rows.running-left: Across eight frames, redraw the left-facing stride cycle while preserving the fastening's true placement and the key's attachment instead of mirroring the finished drawings.
rows.waving: Across four frames, turn toward the viewer, lift an open hand, make one broad greeting sweep and lower the arm into a stable stance.
rows.jumping: Across five frames, crouch, rise about twelve pixels, reach the peak, descend and soften into a stable landing without trails or marks.
rows.failed: Across eight frames, stop with elbows briefly lifted, sink through the knees, hold dropped shoulders and a lowered gaze, then recover slightly while remaining plainly disappointed.
rows.waiting: Across six frames, keep eyes open and hands behind the hips, lean toward the expected action, hold, make one questioning head tilt and return without pacing.
rows.running: Across six frames, stay planted with both forearms forward, prepare the hands, deliberately close and reopen them in an alternating clockwork exercise, check their alignment and reset.
rows.review: Across six frames, turn slightly sideways, raise one wrist toward the face, inspect its wooden joint with the other hand beneath it, hold, nod and finish with a compact task-complete salute.

do_not_resemble: No franchise look-alike, logo, real-person likeness or copied artwork.
A wooden nutcracker soldier reads as the Nutcracker of the ballet and of Disney's film. Give it its own uniform and proportions rather than the ballet's classic nutcracker costume.
brief.why: As The Nutcracker, I chose careful hinges, open hands and a modest salute to express a helpful machine with a warm heart. I assume the soldier can exercise and inspect its existing hand joints without extra equipment; its key remains attached throughout. The compact cap, short uniform and uneven fastening establish its own proportions. Codex's technical decision follows v2: one transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas, eight columns by eleven rows, with 192 × 208 cells and row 0–8 frame counts of 6, 8, 8, 4, 5, 8, 6, 6 and 6; all unused cells remain fully transparent. Retain the sheet's 8 fps as playback guidance, without adding frames to reach two seconds. Keep poses within x=16–176 and y=16–192, with standing feet at y=184, stable scale and body-anchored face placement. Preserve essential inner marks at least two pixels wide and important gaps at least four pixels open. Rows 9 and 10 contain static gaze and pose directions, with the same palette and paint treatment: row 9 is 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5; row 10 is 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5. Angles run clockwise in screen coordinates, with 000 up, 090 right, 180 down and 270 left. Use coordinated head and torso turns so adjacent directions differ visibly. These replace the sheet's sixteen paint variants. The Painter's supplied readability guidance informs the distinct silhouettes: loose arms for idle, hands behind hips and outward lean for waiting, paired forward hands for work, and a raised wrist with sideways inspection for review; carry these distinctions into every later image prompt. No images were supplied for this pet, so no measured function defect or validation result is claimed. Later function flags must identify pet, direction or base treatment, row, frame and visible evidence. Motion measurements remain guidance recorded in provenance; only skill validators gate a rendered pet. No veto is proposed; Originality may veto only in juries and never ranks taste. Paul waived approval steps, retains a later veto, and all assets remain local.

previous.motion_policy: Style-sheet motion numbers (pixel displacement, angles, timing and amplitudes) are drawing guidance. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; a measured difference from style guidance is recorded in provenance, not a reason to fail or spend repairs.

decisions: Previous attempt was inspected and preserved; it contains logs only and no reusable generated art.
Use built-in imagegen sequentially with one art worker; keep every used generated source and its cache path in local logs.
Attach the unchanged family reference to every job; use it for painting treatment only, never ram anatomy or belongings.
Redraw running-left because the off-center fastening and back key must retain physical placement.
Use genuine generated transparency, with the pipeline-selected chroma key retained for deterministic QA and one final despill pass.
Preserve matte herb-green uniform, blue collar, ochre fastening, cream wood, soot edges, rust mouth; no palette variants.
Waiting uses hands behind hips and an expectant lean; work uses planted paired forward hands; review raises and inspects a wrist then salutes.
Look mechanics: planted feet and lower torso remain fixed; neck hinge turns and pitches head, eyes follow the nose, shoulders follow subtly; key stays attached, face remains visible.
Style motion amplitudes are drawing guidance only; measure observed movement after assembly and record it without extra acceptance thresholds.
Use bundled preview timing, whose longer end holds retain the requested calm rhythm; no extra frames to force two-second rows.

Register extracted rows with a shared transform per row: scale 0.74 for ordinary rows and 0.84 for the jump whose extraction viewport includes airspace; register standing soles to y=184. This brings jump physical body size near idle while preserving all source vertical displacement and generous safe padding.

Combine the COMPLETE unaltered family and standard contact sheets side-by-side with labels in references/family-and-standard.png to stay within five image references without dropping either visual. Labels are reference-only.

Observed jump sole lift is [0, 7, 27, 8, 0] px versus guidance 10–14/about 12 px; it clearly crouches, rises and lands, retaining the intended hop. Idle top bounds are [35, 36, 36, 34, 36, 35] versus 1–2 px breathing guidance, with one blink and a restrained tilt. These observations add no acceptance gate.

Labeled look review accepts subtle steps at 067.5, 157.5, 202.5 and 315 as warnings: intended quadrants remain visible and the loop does not reverse. The 157.5→180 continuity outlier reflects head pitch/foreshortening with planted boots and attached key, not a visible registration jump.

Three independent read-only blind reviewers were used under the skill; strict-majority bundled validation passed every tested axis. An independent labeled final review passed with warnings about similar intermediate looks and general hand activity.

Export lossless RGBA WebP and a quality-78 compressed contact WebP. Final previews are extracted from the exact final WebP: nine state GIFs, all-state GIF/MP4, native idle-jump-idle GIF/MP4, look-loop GIF/MP4, four labeled stills and contact/direction sheets.

Final bundled jump measurement uses alpha>16 and reports 28 px lift with 1 px landing delta; all-alpha observation reports 27 px lift and exact y=184 registration. Both retain the intended jump and do not enforce the style amplitude.

Retain all 18 generated sources in sources/ and record original cache paths, SHA-256 hashes, exact prompts/inputs and repair history in logs/provenance.json; no whole-pet redo, service mutation, or Library operation occurred.

contract:
The v2 sprite-sheet contract fixes 192 × 208 cells, eight columns by eleven rows,
one transparent 1536 × 2288 atlas. The nine animation rows (0–8) have these exact frame counts:
idle 6, running-right 8, running-left 8, waving 4, jumping 5, failed 8, waiting 6,
running 6 (focused work, not locomotion), review 6. Unused cells stay fully transparent.
Rows 9 and 10 hold sixteen look directions, eight per row, clockwise in screen coordinates:
row 9: 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5;
row 10: 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5.
000 is up, 090 right, 180 down, 270 left. These are gaze/pose directions with the same
palette and treatment, not sixteen palette variants, paint treatments or separate animations.
motion_policy: Style-sheet motion numbers (pixel displacement, angles, timing and amplitudes) are drawing guidance. Only the skill's validators gate a pet; a measured difference from style guidance is recorded in provenance, not a reason to fail or spend repairs.

contract_overrides.original: Each row has 16 frames at 8 fps: two seconds, four beats of four frames. Repeat held drawings within that grid.
contract_overrides.replacement: Rows 0–8 contain 6, 8, 8, 4, 5, 8, 6, 6, 6 frames respectively. Preserve 8 fps as drawing guidance; use bundled preview durations and holds, without adding frames for two seconds.
contract_overrides.reason: V2 fixes frame counts; the bundled renderer supplies state-specific timing.

contract_overrides.original: V2 adds sixteen selectable looks to the base sheet, each covering all nine rows and all twenty seeds. These change paint handling and small accents, never creature, costume or props: 1. Dry Paint—sparse broad grain; 2. Full Paint—solid matte fills; 3. Thin Paint—slightly translucent fills; 4. Broken Edge—small fixed gaps in solid-body outlines; 5. Soft Edge—gentler edge transitions; 6. Firm Edge—clearer shape boundaries; 7. Cream Edge—a narrow light-facing rim; 8. Soot Edge—a deeper inward border; 9. Ochre Touch—ochre on existing small accents; 10. Rust Touch—rust on existing small accents; 11. Herb Touch—green on existing small accents; 12. Blue Touch—blue on existing small accents; 13. Pale Paint—lighter secondary colors; 14. Deep Paint—darker secondary colors; 15. Quiet Paint—less saturated secondary colors; 16. Fresh Paint—stronger secondary colors.
contract_overrides.replacement: Sixteen static gaze/pose directions with unchanged palette and material: row 9 = 000, 022.5, 045, 067.5, 090, 112.5, 135, 157.5; row 10 = 180, 202.5, 225, 247.5, 270, 292.5, 315, 337.5. Clockwise screen coordinates: up=000, right=090, down=180, left=270.
contract_overrides.reason: V2 defines directional looks, not paint variants or additional animation sheets.
